title: Privilege escalation — name the abuse
description:
Amaka: 'The Griot did not exploit a kernel CVE. They did not steal `root`'s password. They abused a feature — a feature your colleague added two days before the breach, marked "temporary diagnostic". Tell me which feature, how it works, and what they typed inside an interactive program to turn it into a root shell.'

Write an analyst note (220+ words) that:

1. **Quotes the sudoers entry** that enabled the abuse, from the exact `/evidence/fs/...` path. One line, in a code block.

2. **Names the feature being abused.** The escalation does not depend on a software bug — it depends on a documented feature of one of the binaries in that sudoers entry. Name the binary, name the feature (a single keystroke / command inside an interactive program), and explain in one sentence why allowing it under `NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/<binary> /var/log/*` is equivalent to giving the user full `sudo ALL`.

3. **Names the GTFOBins entry** for the abused binary (full URL `https://gtfobins.github.io/gtfobins/<name>/`) and quote the specific GTFOBins technique label (e.g. `Sudo`).

4. **Names the MITRE ATT&CK sub-technique** — `T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching`. Quote it in full.

5. **Proposes the fix — two parts:**
   - **Immediate:** what makes `<binary> /var/log/*` unsafe under NOPASSWD, and what a *safe scoped* entry would look like (e.g. `journalctl -u nginx`, or a wrapper script that only opens specific files in `cat`-mode without shell escape).
   - **Structural:** why "temporary diagnostic" sudo grants need a documented expiry, a code-review gate, and an automated audit (cite the policy reference and the tool — `sudoers` `Defaults timestamp_timeout`, AWS SSM Session Manager as an alternative to long-lived sudo, etc.).

6. **One mistake I almost made:** 40+ word section. The seductive wrong answer is "the user shouldn't have been in sudoers at all" — explain why that misses the point (the dangerous part is the *what*, not the *who*; the same entry would be safe for a different binary).

**Citation bar:**
- GTFOBins URL with the binary name.
- MITRE technique ID in full (`T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching`).
- One external reference on sudo hardening — NIST SP 800-53r5 AC-6(9) (Auditing Use of Privileged Functions), CIS Linux Benchmark §5.2/§5.3, or the `sudoers(5)` man page §SUDOERS_LDAP.

Submission: in-platform.

---

**Universal grading rule.** Generic answers fail. Every claim in your submission must be tied to specific evidence — an artefact from the lab (file path, log line, command output, payload, screenshot) **and** at least one external citation where research is relevant (NIST section number, MITRE technique ID, CVE, vendor advisory, ISO control ID, NDPA section). Claims without an attached artefact, timestamp, payload, standard section, or business constraint earn zero for that claim. Lab-only answers earn partial credit. External-only answers earn partial credit. Full credit requires both.
